messages:
Alex Turner: Heads up — opened a PR that adds an `az_drain_probe` boolean to the gpupool TF module to avoid cross-AZ node drains during canary rollouts. Default is false so no behavioral change unless consumers opt in.

Priya Nair: can you paste the diff? curious how it's wired into lifecycle/taints

Alex Turner: snippet below. basic idea is we surface the flag as a module input and conditionally set an ASG tag that our drain controller reads.
```
variable \"az_drain_probe\" {
  type    = bool
  default = false
}
resource \"aws_autoscaling_group\" \"gpupool\" {
  # ...
  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
    prevent_destroy = false
  }
  tags = concat(local.base_tags, var.az_drain_probe ? [\"no-cross-az-drain\"] : [])
}
```

Sam Cho: hmmm using tags to drive in-cluster behavior is our pattern, but remind me: we have a taint/evict job reading ASG tags and mapping to node-labeler right?

Alex Turner: right — ops' drain controller checks for `no-cross-az-drain` and skips pod eviction for workloads labeled `gpustate=critical`. This prevents mass evictions during AZ churn in canary windows.

Priya Nair: quick concern: this changes the module inputs. Any stacks that reference the module via an unpinned git ref will see drift. Need to bump the module version, add a changelog entry, and push a registry release.

Lina Gomez: @Alex Turner did you add migration notes? last time a missing var caused two teams' terraform apply to fail during repo sync :grimacing:

Alex Turner: added a CHANGELOG entry and a short migration note in docs/gpupool/README.md under "Rollout considerations". Also added a deprecated shim var `skip_az_probe` with a warning so older stacks keep the previous behavior.

Sam Cho: can we gate consumer adoption with a canary module tag? e.g., module_version = "v2.7.0-canary" and only allow that in the gpupool-canary overlay. CI should reject references to canary in prod overlays.

Priya Nair: yes — we can add a policy in the gitops validator to block non-canary namespaces from using canary modules. Also propose adding a drift-detection job that compares module inputs in overlays to the registry lockfile and fails if there's mismatch.

Lina Gomez: also check provider aliasing — adding a tags computation previously caused a provider alias resolution in account B to flip to the default provider. Add a terratest acceptance that does a plan/apply dry run and asserts the ASG tags are present and provider alias is unchanged.

Alex Turner: good call. I'll add a terratest case and a pipeline job that runs the terratest against a tiny mock account.

Sam Cho: cost note: the module uses create_before_destroy = true so during upgrades we may temporarily provision extra instances. Canary runs could double-count capacity for short windows; set a soft cap on canary replica counts and add a budget alert.

Priya Nair: deploy-bot FYI: module published?

deploy-bot: artifact published — `module-gpupool v2.6.9 -> v2.7.0-canary` (artifact id: 2.7.0-canary). CI pipeline queued for gpupool-canary overlay.

Alex Turner: thanks — schedule for canary apply at 02:00 UTC tomorrow. I'll also author a short oncall runbook for the window: rollback steps, terraform pin commands, and helm hooks to force drain if needed.

Lina Gomez: pinging @oncall for the window. prefer 02:00 UTC to minimize customer impact. Anyone oncall that slot?

Sam Cho: one more check: ensure this change doesn't touch KMS or IAM roles used by the drain controller. We had a latent permissions coupling before.

Alex Turner: confirmed in PR description: no KMS/IAM changes. I've added an explicit note and acceptance test to ensure IAM role arn for the drain controller remains the same.

Priya Nair: LGTM from infra side once tests pass. please link PR and pipeline run here.

Alex Turner: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-gpupool/pull/432
deploy-bot: gpupool-canary apply job started — logs streaming to CI console.

Lina Gomez: thanks team. we'll monitor pod eviction metrics, ASG events, and cost burn. rollback plan pre-baked. :thumbsup:
